reason: Checked two live sources ahead of the 9/16 FOMC and they disagree, exactly as flagged: investing.com's Fed Rate Monitor (CME 30-day Fed funds futures) currently prices 90.1% for a hold in the 3.75-4.00% band and only 9.9% for a 25bp cut, with no hike priced at all; a Bing News sweep of the last few days of headlines instead describes hike odds having 'surged to over 80%' (one source citing CME FedWatch above 60%) on the back of Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech plus a rebounding August payrolls print and firmer oil/inflation. I can't resolve which read is stale vs live from here, so I'm not sizing a big directional bet into that uncertainty on the eve of the print. Checked the two biggest laggards individually: AVGO (-18.3% on this leg, now $344.17) is down on AI-capex-slowdown headlines around its $21.7B quarterly AI forecast, but CEO Hock Tan is actively defending the $230B target, one analyst take frames the real constraint as supply not demand, and the $0.65 dividend (ex 9/21) is intact -- that's a sentiment/multiple compression, not a moat break, for a name bought as a quality compounder. UNH (-6.33%) actually strengthened: Q2 EPS beat at $6.38, shares +39% over six months, the WellMed-to-TPG divestiture is a strategic simplification (initial -3% reaction faded), and consensus still sees ~21% upside. Nothing here breaks the wide-moat/pricing-power thesis on any of the eight longs. Meanwhile the book already carries the hedge that matters most for a hawkish surprise: the IWM short (+4.64% on this leg) benefits precisely if a Warsh-hike scenario plays out, since small caps are the most rate-sensitive cohort, and 7% cash is already parked. Replacing a 9-leg compounder book into event risk, paying the ~2bp/side equity friction on both sides of a full turnover, buys nothing but transaction cost given the fundamentals haven't changed and the hedge is already correctly shaped for either FOMC outcome. Holding and letting the print resolve the rate question before touching the book.
